title: Singleton influence identities
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ and let $i$ be a coordinate. The uniform probability that flipping coordinate $i$ changes $f$ equals the coalitional influence of the singleton $\{i\}$, and this influence is twice the coalitional influence toward either output: $\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)=\operatorname{Inf}_{\{i\}}(f)=2\operatorname{Inf}_{\{i\},+1}(f)=2\operatorname{Inf}_{\{i\},-1}(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
